spec: PLAN.md 3.39.2 with the implementation deviations recorded in PLAN.md 3.39.12 (compact reconstructible commit; derivable fields removed from the payload; constant AAD; history before error-correction level); implemented in src/secutg/v2/join/
notes: V2Q:<code>:<nonce_b64url>:<ct_b64url>. <code> is exactly 32 characters of 0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ (upper case, no separators, no I/L/O/U leniency); <nonce> is 24 bytes; <ct> at least the 16-byte tag. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed.
key = BLAKE2b-256("tg-v2-join-v1" || base32decode(code)); XChaCha20-Poly1305-IETF; AAD = "secutg/v2join/v1" (constant: binding_id is inside the ciphertext, the scanner cannot know it beforehand).

plaintext is JSON with EXACTLY these keys in EXACTLY this order and no whitespace: v(=1), kind(="v2join"), peer_user_id, binding_id, epoch(number), safety_code, roster[[identity_pk, encapsulation_pk], ...] (2-element string arrays, ascending device_id, at least 2), masters[m_e, m_(e-1), ...] (base64url strings; masters[i] is generation epoch-i; 1..epoch entries), new_device{label, identity_seed(32B), encapsulation_sk(32B)}, commit{event_id(16B), created_ms, expires_ms (decimal strings), actor(number: index into roster), packages[roster.length+1 base64url], sig(64B)}, expires_ms(number). Any other key, order, or type is malformed.

Derived on the reader: device_id = base64url(sha256(identity_pk)) for each roster entry (they MUST be strictly ascending, else malformed); the new device: crypto_sign_seed_keypair(identity_seed) gives identity_pk / the 64-byte sk, crypto_scalarmult_base(encapsulation_sk) gives encapsulation_pk, device_id as above (it MUST not be in the roster); actor_device = roster[actor].device_id; packages[i] belongs to roster[i], packages[last] to the new device.

commit is COMPACT (deviation from the plan's verbatim wire: that form measures ~3.8 KB and no QR holds it). The scanner rebuilds the P2 ROSTER_COMMIT: envelope {v:"2", type:"ROSTER_COMMIT", event_id, chat_id=peer_user_id, actor_user=<own account id>, actor_device, created_ms, expires_ms, body, sig} with body {reason:"add_device", binding_id, epoch=String(epoch+1), device_roster=sorted(roster device_ids + new_device_id), packages=[{device_id: id, package: <the package derived for id>} for id in device_roster], new_device{device_id,identity_pk,encapsulation_pk}}, SJ-serialised (sorted keys), "P2:" + base64url(utf8(SJ)). It MUST verify under roster[actor].identity_pk (domain "secuTG/v2/P2") BEFORE anything else is believed, else the whole code is malformed. expect.commit_wire is the exact text the scanner must send into the chat.
Errors, in this order: malformed (syntax / payload / derivation / signature), undecryptable (AEAD), wrong_chat (peer_user_id != the chat scanned in), expired (now_ms > expires_ms + 120000).

Capacity: QR byte mode. ECC M holds 2331 bytes, ECC L 2953. History wins over the error correction level: for k = 0, 1, 2, ... OLDEST history masters dropped, if the text fits M use M, else if it fits L use L, else drop one more; only when the current master alone exceeds L is the code too large. Measured on these vectors: a 2-device roster with the current master alone is 1618 bytes; each history master adds 62 bytes; each extra roster device adds 272 bytes; with no history the roster fits M up to 4 devices and L up to 6 devices. The fit cases pin the exact numbers.

Deterministic packages: the sealed box for device_roster[i] (the COMMIT's sorted order) is crypto_box_seal built by hand with the ephemeral secret seal_ephemeral_sk_hex(i) = byte(0x80+i)*32: epk = scalarmult_base(esk); nonce = blake2b-24(epk||rpk); epk || crypto_box_easy(master, nonce, rpk, esk). A client need not reproduce the sealing to pass: decoding to expect and opening its own package with crypto_box_seal_open is normative.

Actors: ed25519 keys from crypto_sign_seed_keypair(seed); x25519 pk = scalarmult_base(sk). master of epoch e = byte(0x40+e)*32. now_ms is the scanner's clock for every case unless the case sets its own.
